title: The process fails to boot when a required secret is absent; degrades on an optional absent secret
description: At boot the Secrets Manager client attempts to materialise every name in the declared slice. A `required: true` entry that cannot be resolved for the active environment aborts boot with a stable-coded error naming the logical name and the environment, and no partial start-up state is exposed on any port. A `required: false` entry that cannot be resolved is served as null; consumers that call `get` on an optional name handle the null branch. The failure mode is loud, early, and irreversible in-boot; there is no wait-and-retry loop that would leave the process half-alive with silently missing secrets.
rationale: A process that starts with a required secret missing serves broken traffic while the operator hunts a null-pointer stack trace ten layers down. Failing at boot names the problem exactly once at exactly the right layer, and the operator moves straight to the manifest.
